Limpieza del texto

  1. Todo a minusculas.
  2. Quitar símbolos de puntuación.
  3. Quitar numeros
  4. Quitar stopwords
  5. Quitar espacios en blanco redundantes
library(readr)
## 
## Adjuntando el paquete: 'readr'
## The following object is masked from 'package:koRpus':
## 
##     tokenize
corpus_processed <- tm_map(corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
# inspect(corpus_processed[1])
corpus_processed <- tm_map(corpus_processed, removePunctuation)
# inspect(corpus_processed[1])
corpus_processed <- tm_map(corpus_processed, removeNumbers)
# inspect(corpus_processed[1])
corpus_processed <- tm_map(corpus_processed, removeWords, stopwords("english"))
# inspect(corpus_processed[1])
corpus_processed <- tm_map(corpus_processed, stripWhitespace)
#i nspect(corpus_processed[1])

Stemming

corpus_stemmed <- corpus_processed
corpus_stemmed <- tm_map(corpus_stemmed, stemDocument)

Creamos la matriz DTM.

  frec = as.numeric(frecuencias_ordenadas)

Tokkenización.

texts <- sapply(corpus_processed, as.character)
anno  <- udpipe_annotate(ud, x = texts, doc_id = seq_along(texts))
anno  <- as.data.frame(anno)

lemmatized_docs <- anno %>%
  group_by(doc_id) %>%
  summarise(text = paste(lemma, collapse = " ")) %>%
  pull(text)

#Corpus con lemmatización
(corpus_lemmatized <- VCorpus(VectorSource(lemmatized_docs)))
## <<VCorpus>>
## Metadata:  corpus specific: 0, document level (indexed): 0
## Content:  documents: 994

Segmentación de oraciones y análisis de longitud

# ==============================================================================
# Segmentamos en oraciones y analizamos su longitud
# ==============================================================================
library(tokenizers)
library(ggplot2)

# Tokenizar en oraciones
oraciones <- tokenize_sentences(reviews_text)

# Longitud de cada oración (número de palabras)
longitudes <- lengths(oraciones)

df_oraciones <- tibble(
  oracion      = seq_along(longitudes),
  num_palabras = longitudes
)

# Gráfico de longitud de oraciones
ggplot(df_oraciones, aes(x = oracion, y = num_palabras)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Longitud de oraciones (número de palabras)",
    x     = "Número de oración",
    y     = "Número de palabras"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

# ==============================================================================
# Detección de idioma de cada oración
# ==============================================================================
library(textcat)

idiomas <- textcat(oraciones)
print(table(idiomas))

Lexicón Bing

# ==============================================================================
# Frecuencia de palabras y detección de positividad con lexicón Bing
# ==============================================================================
# Tokenización de todo el corpus
palabras <- tokenize_words(reviews_text)

tabla <- table(unlist(palabras))
tabla <- tibble(
  word     = names(tabla),
  recuento = as.numeric(tabla)
) %>% 
  anti_join(tibble(word = stopwords("en")), by = "word") %>% 
  arrange(desc(recuento))

# Palabras positivas según Bing
pos <- get_sentiments("bing") %>% filter(sentiment == "positive")
pos_reviews <- tabla %>% semi_join(pos, by = "word")

# Visualizamos las 15 palabras positivas más frecuentes
pos_reviews %>% 
  slice_max(order_by = recuento, n = 15) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(word, recuento), y = recuento)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title = "Palabras positivas más frecuentes (lexicón Bing)",
      x     = NULL, 
      y     = "Frecuencia"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

Lexicón NRC

# ==============================================================================
# Emociones con lexicón NRC
# ==============================================================================
# Obtiene para cada reseña un vector de 10 emociones
nrc_matrix <- syuzhet::get_nrc_sentiment(reviews_text, language = "english")

# Suma total por emoción (columnas)
emo_totals <- colSums(nrc_matrix)

# Data frame para graficar
emo_df <- data.frame(
  emocion    = names(emo_totals),
  frecuencia = as.numeric(emo_totals),
  row.names  = NULL
)

# Gráfico de barras horizontal
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(emo_df, aes(x = emocion, y = frecuencia, fill = emocion)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Frecuencia de emociones (lexicón NRC - syuzhet)",
       x     = NULL,
       y     = "Frecuencia") +
  theme_minimal()

# ==============================================================================
# Gráfico radial de emociones (lexicón NRC vía syuzhet)
# ==============================================================================
library(ggplot2)

# Usamos emo_df (emocion + frecuencia) creado en el chunk 'nrc'
emo_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = emocion, y = frecuencia, fill = emocion)) +
    geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
    coord_polar(start = 0) +
    labs(
      title = "Distribución radial de emociones (NRC - syuzhet)",
      x     = NULL,
      y     = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid  = element_blank()
    )

Wordcloud de emociones

# ==============================================================================
# Wordcloud de emociones usando emo_df 
# ==============================================================================
library(wordcloud)

set.seed(123)
wordcloud(
  words        = emo_df$emocion,     # emociones únicas
  freq         = emo_df$frecuencia,  # frecuencias agregadas
  min.freq     = 1,                  # filtra afectados
  random.order = FALSE,
  rot.per      = 0.0,                # sin rotación
  scale        = c(4, 0.5),          # escalado de tamaño

)

N-gramas y redes de co‑ocurrencia

bigramas <- tibble(texto = reviews_text) %>% 
  unnest_tokens(bigram, texto, token = "ngrams", n = 2) %>% 
  count(bigram, sort = TRUE)

bigramas_limpios <- bigramas %>% 
  separate(bigram, c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") %>% 
  filter(!word1 %in% stopwords("en")) %>% 
  filter(!word2 %in% stopwords("en")) %>% 
  unite(bigram, word1, word2, sep = " ")
g_bigram <- bigramas_limpios %>% 
  filter(n > 2) %>% 
  separate(bigram, c("from", "to"), sep = " ") %>% 
  graph_from_data_frame()

set.seed(123)
ggraph(g_bigram, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm")), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_node_point(size = 0) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), size = 3) +
  theme_void()

TOPIC MODELLING

library(topicmodels)
## Warning: package 'topicmodels' was built under R version 4.4.3
library(RColorBrewer)
library(wordcloud)
library(remotes)
## Warning: package 'remotes' was built under R version 4.4.3
library(tm)
library(ggplot2)
library(ldatuning)

Previamente hemos ejecutado las siguientes líneas para saber el número de tópicos a escoger.

minFreq <- 5
DTM <- DocumentTermMatrix(corpus_stemmed, control = list(bounds = list(global = c(minFreq, Inf))))

# Eliminamos documentos vacíos
sel <- slam::row_sums(DTM) > 0
DTM <- DTM[sel, ]

result <- ldatuning::FindTopicsNumber(
  DTM,
  topics = seq(from = 2, to = 20, by = 4),
  metrics = c("CaoJuan2009",  "Deveaud2014"),
  method = "Gibbs",
  control = list(seed = 77),
  verbose = TRUE
)
## fit models... done.
## calculate metrics:
##   CaoJuan2009... done.
##   Deveaud2014... done.
FindTopicsNumber_plot(result)
## Warning: The `<scale>` argument of `guides()` cannot be `FALSE`. Use "none" instead as
## of ggplot2 3.3.4.
## ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the ldatuning package.
##   Please report the issue at <https://github.com/nikita-moor/ldatuning/issues>.
## This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
## generated.

El punto ideal sería escoger dos topics pero consideramos que son pocos. Por ende escogeremos k=10 que presenta un buen equilibrio en las dos métricas escogidas.

K <- 10

set.seed(1234)

topicModel <- LDA(dtm_stemmed, K, method="Gibbs", control=list(iter = 500, verbose = 25,alpha=0.2))
## K = 10; V = 2467; M = 994
## Sampling 500 iterations!
## Iteration 25 ...
## Iteration 50 ...
## Iteration 75 ...
## Iteration 100 ...
## Iteration 125 ...
## Iteration 150 ...
## Iteration 175 ...
## Iteration 200 ...
## Iteration 225 ...
## Iteration 250 ...
## Iteration 275 ...
## Iteration 300 ...
## Iteration 325 ...
## Iteration 350 ...
## Iteration 375 ...
## Iteration 400 ...
## Iteration 425 ...
## Iteration 450 ...
## Iteration 475 ...
## Iteration 500 ...
## Gibbs sampling completed!
topicModel
## A LDA_Gibbs topic model with 10 topics.
attr(topicModel,"alpha")
## [1] 0.2
tmResult <- posterior(topicModel)

attributes(tmResult)
## $names
## [1] "terms"  "topics"
beta <- tmResult$terms   
dim(beta)
## [1]   10 2467
theta <- tmResult$topics 
dim(theta)             
## [1] 994  10
terms(topicModel, 10)
##       Topic 1    Topic 2     Topic 3  Topic 4      Topic 5     Topic 6   
##  [1,] "video"    "print"     "cours"  "cours"      "cours"     "cours"   
##  [2,] "student"  "great"     "excel"  "understand" "much"      "will"    
##  [3,] "question" "ableton"   "great"  "week"       "learn"     "one"

vizDataFrame <- reshape2::melt(
  cbind(data.frame(topicProportionExamples),
        document = factor(1:N)),
  variable.name = "topic",
  id.vars = "document")

ggplot(data = vizDataFrame, aes(topic, value, fill = document), ylab = "proportion") +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~document, ncol = N)
